messages.subject: gl.Pca() & gl.pcoa() give different results
parts:
Hi there,

I am hoping someone can help me.

I am trying to perform a PCA on a genlight object. I have used gl.Pca() and gl.pcoa() but each function returns different $scores.

It is my understanding that gl.pcoa is a wrapper of gl.Pca, so I am confused about how each return different scores? How can I determine which one is giving me the correct answer?

Here is the code I am using. (I haven't decided whether or not I need to scale and centre my data yet, hence the two versions of glPca).

male.pca1 <- glPca(male.gl, center = TRUE, scale = TRUE, nf = NULL, loadings = TRUE,
                     alleleAsUnit = FALSE, useC = TRUE, parallel = FALSE,
                     n.cores = NULL, returnDotProd=FALSE, matDotProd=NULL)

male.pca2 <- glPca(male.gl, center = FALSE, scale = FALSE, nf = NULL, loadings = TRUE,
                           alleleAsUnit = FALSE, useC = TRUE, parallel = FALSE,
                           n.cores = NULL, returnDotProd=FALSE, matDotProd=NULL)

male.pca3 <- gl.pcoa(male.gl, nfactors= 4)

Many thanks,
Lana

Many thanks,
Lana

messages.author: 9e12eec50c435b60
messages.subject: Re: [dartR] Re: gl.Pca() & gl.pcoa() give different results
parts:
Hi Lana,

Here is the code I use to call glPCA inside gl.pcoa()

pca <-  glPca(gl,
                  nf = 5,
                  parallel = FALSE,
                  n.cores = 16)

The defaults adopted by glPCA when this call is made are 

center = TRUE, 
scale = FALSE,

loadings = TRUE,
alleleAsUnit = FALSE,

useC = TRUE, 
returnDotProd=FALSE, 
matDotProd=NULL

If you want to check the equivalency of the two, you will need to run
male.pca3 <- gl.pcoa(male.gl, nfactors= 4)

against

male.pca2 <- glPca(male.gl, center = TRUE, scale = FALSE, nf = 4, loadings = TRUE,
alleleAsUnit = FALSE, useC = TRUE, parallel = FALSE,

n.cores = 16, returnDotProd=FALSE, matDotProd=NULL)

Can you do that and get back to me?

All the best, Arthur
